ch22.d.preset: Starting arrangement of the charges (drag to move; drag out of the tray at the lower left to add; drop on the bin or double-click to remove)
ch22.d.view: Draw the field as grid arrows, field lines, or both
ch22.d.test: Test charge $q_0$ and the Coulomb forces on it (each charge's force and the net force)
ch22.goal.field: Electric field: the force per unit charge on a test charge at each point, $\vec E = \vec F / q_0$
ch22.goal.super: Superposition: the field of several charges is the vector sum of the fields of each charge
ch22.obs.drag: Drag a charge and the whole field updates at once. Field lines leave positive charges and end on negative ones
ch22.obs.tray: Tray at the lower left: drag a charge out to add it ($+1$, $+2$, $-1$, $-2$ nC); drop it on the tray (bin) or double-click (double-tap) it to remove it
ch22.obs.dipole: Dipole: the field is strongest between the charges and falls off quickly farther away
ch22.obs.like: Like pair: a point of zero field midway between the charges; the field lines push each other apart
ch22.obs.plates: Parallel plates: in the middle between the rows the field points almost the same way (from the $+$ row to the $-$ row); its strength is lowest midway and grows toward each row. Outside, the fields of the two rows point opposite ways and partly cancel
ch22.obs.test: Test charge: the vector sum of the Coulomb forces of the charges (thin arrows) is the net force $\vec F$ (thick arrow), of size $F = q_0 E$
ch22.as.units: Charges in nC, lengths in m
ch22.as.test: Test charge $q_0 = +1$ nC. Source charges are held fixed (the force of the test charge on them is ignored)
ch22.as.log: Grid arrow length is a log scale of the field strength (over three decades); the direction is exact
ch22.as.force: Force arrows share a linear scale set by the largest force (all shortened by the same factor where one would cover a charge). With 7 or more charges only the net force is drawn
ch22.as.plates: Each plate is a row of 8 point charges. A row of point charges acts like a charged rod, not a sheet: a uniform field needs plates much wider than their gap with the charge spread evenly over the surface. The number of field lines is proportional to the charge (10 per nC)
ch22.as.sym: $k = 1/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$ = 8.99×10⁹ N·m²/C²: Coulomb constant, $\varepsilon_0$ = 8.85×10⁻¹² C²/(N·m²): permittivity of free space. $\hat r_i$: unit vector (length 1, direction only) from the $i$-th charge $q_i$ toward the test charge, $r_i$: the distance between them. $q_1$: the charge nearest to the test charge (labelled on the stage), $F_1$: the size of its force on the test charge
